narrative_profile: psychological thriller-romance with dual-layered cat-and-mouse structure; single first-person POV (Calder); slow-burn romance emerging from surveillance violation; domestic gaslighting as central crime; evidence-based climax without violence.
title_working: The Things I Let Him See
surface_case: A surveillance operative hired to document a separated wife's instability becomes obsessed with her ordinary routines, unaware she is aware of his observation. As her husband's manipulation escalates toward forcing a property settlement, the watcher must decide whether to protect the woman directing his gaze or preserve the evidence that will free her.
true_case: Grant Hart has manufactured a pattern of instability around Lena for seven weeks before Chapter One via duplicate mailbox key, master-access credential, admin control of footage and incident records, and timed environmental disturbances. Calder is hired for 21 days of surveillance and independently retains unedited originals. Lena detects Calder in Chapter Three, controls what he sees via diagnostic tests (folded red receipts, doorframe seals, paper planner, repeated routines, certified honeytoken envelope), and builds an evidence chain that culminates in Grant exposing his own false chain of custody at the settlement. Calder's attraction develops through observation; Lena's attraction begins only after confrontation and negotiated consent in Chapters Nine–Ten. The romance is earned only after the surveillance contract, evidence dependency, and immediate threat end — Lena asks Calder to return without recording equipment after he has transferred evidence out of his sole custody and accepted her refusal to let him decide for her.
core_question: Who controls what is seen — and does seeing give ownership?
emotional_question: Can a relationship born from violation become chosen rather than engineered?
book1_promise: Lena will defeat Grant's control without being physically rescued; Calder will prove his loyalty by preserving evidence rather than possessing her; the romance will be earned only after all power imbalances are dismantled.
case_closed: Grant's manipulation is exposed at the settlement via contradictory evidence (envelope chain of custody, unedited footage, access audit, field notebook, planner, contract). Lena retains her apartment; Grant loses admin access; evidence enters official custody; legal proceedings continue but Grant no longer controls Lena's environment.
series_door_opened: Mae gives Lena a sealed archived complaint from another condominium that used the same security vendor, predating Grant's board position and describing short camera gaps paired with resident instability reports. Lena does not open it during Book One.
book2_hook: A sealed complaint from another condominium using the same security vendor, predating Grant's board role, describing short camera gaps paired with resident instability reports — suggesting the mechanism existed before Grant learned to exploit it. Lena chooses whether to investigate or leave the surveillance world behind.
book1_ending_type: romantic resolution after full independence — Lena grants Calder chosen, conditional access without recording equipment; thriller question resolved (Lena controlled the decisive visible sequence); legal aftermath ongoing but Grant's active control ended.
reader_payoff_book1: The watcher is watched; the victim is the strategist; the romance is earned only after all dependencies end; the climax is won by evidence and planning, not violence or confession.
